correctness.rationale: All q range endpoints verified by explicit block decompositions. The digit complement formula and Legendre factorial identity prove every term has valuation a, and a self-contained integer forward-difference argument rules out all other gcd primes. 21 prime-power instances, 1136 valuation checks and 164 direct binomials cross-checked by a standalone checker. The finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact value D(p^a-1)=p^a and uniform valuations for every multiplier are not implied by the unit-gcd criterion or prime-support condition of Guo et al. 2026: knowing p divides a gcd does not establish its precise exponent. Hong 2016 concerns a different indexing family. Checks of the fully accessible primary source and targeted research-record queries found no equivalent proposition. Residual implicit-priority risk is expressly recognized.
residual_risks: Simple Legendre digit-sum identities may have been implicitly observed by earlier authors without an indexed exact statement.
No independent priority audit; indexing/search cannot prove worldwide novelty.
The result is scoped to the prime-power-index family and does not resolve full gcd values for all k.

value.rationale: This exact natural gcd invariant is the quantitative prime-power case of the recently solved OEIS A080170 gcd support problem. Uniform valuation across every multiplier is a nontrivial additional structural property, not merely another gcd>1 witness. The prime-power condition is mathematically intrinsic to the existing theorem rather than an unmotivated finite slice. The limitation to prime powers and possible elementary earlier implicit derivations are explicitly acknowledged.
